chunks: From him, from more than one, from Abu al-Mi'za, from al-Halabi and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the slaughtered meat of the Murji'ah and the Haruriyah, so he said: 'Eat it, and be firm and settled until what happens happens.'
As for what is sold in the markets of the Muslims, there is no harm in eating it, even if you do not know who slaughtered it. This was narrated.
ai.seo_question: Is the meat of specific Shia sects like the Murji'ah and Haruriyah considered halal to eat?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that the meat of the Murji'ah and Haruriyah sects is permissible to eat, specifically noting that meat sold in general Muslim markets is considered halal even if the specific identity of the slaughterer is unknown. This ruling reflects the Shia principle of *istishab al-halaliyyah* (presumption of permissibility) in commercial transactions, where the default status of food remains pure unless proven otherwise. It highlights the practical flexibility in distinguishing between theological deviation and ritual impurity in daily consumption.
